statement: A video service streams a movie at an average rate of $3$ megabits per second. Using $1$ byte $= 8$ bits and $1$ gigabyte $= 1{,}000$ megabytes, how many gigabytes of data does a $2$-hour movie use?

choices.misconception: I changed 2 hours into 120, which is the number of minutes, and used it as the number of seconds.
I divided the megabits by 1,000 to get gigabytes but never divided by 8 to turn bits into bytes.
I multiplied by 8 to change bits to bytes, but a byte is bigger than a bit, so I should have divided by 8.

hints: Find the total number of megabits first. How many seconds are in $2$ hours?
$2$ hours is $7{,}200$ seconds, so the movie uses $3 \cdot 7{,}200 = 21{,}600$ megabits. Now change bits to bytes.

solutions.reliable: Two hours is $2 \cdot 60 \cdot 60 = 7{,}200$ seconds, so the movie uses $3 \cdot 7{,}200 = 21{,}600$ megabits. Each byte is $8$ bits, so that is $21{,}600 \div 8 = 2{,}700$ megabytes, and $2{,}700 \div 1{,}000 = 2.7$ gigabytes.
solutions.elegant: Chain the units so they cancel: $\frac{3 \text{ Mb}}{1 \text{ s}} \cdot 7{,}200 \text{ s} \cdot \frac{1 \text{ MB}}{8 \text{ Mb}} \cdot \frac{1 \text{ GB}}{1{,}000 \text{ MB}} = 2.7 \text{ GB}$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
